newsitem.title: UK: London BFI continues to climb, Panamaxes boom.
newsitem.headline: London BFI continues to climb, Panamaxes boom.

text.p: The BFI cleared the 1300 barrier with something to spare today, up 15 points to 1311, a level last seen on June 10.
That extended the gain to 311 points for October alone and in turn has transformed fortunes for the Panamax sector.
A month ago poor demand for scrap, rising bunker prices and a weak freight market combined to persuade many owners of Panamaxes over 10 years old to consider laying up.
Today booming demand in most traditional Panamax loading areas with the exception of South America offers profitable trading opportunities to all but the oldest and most uneconomical Panamax vessels.
Some market observers have reservations about the scope for further improvement in the Atlantic but few regard the Pacific as having reached its peak yet.
After a significant delay following the Panamax lead, there are now clear signs of a revival also in conditions for Capers worldwide.

Brokers believe few of these types remain open for loading before the end of the year. There is little apparent change in the handy-size situation - a firm market in the north Atlantic with generally sluggish conditions elsewhere.
GRAIN --Large numbers of shipbrokers are in Hamburg for the annual celebrations and there was little reported in key grain trades U.S. Gulf/Continent or U.S. Gulf/Japan.

Cobelfret was said to have paid only $12.50 for 59,000 hss Mississippi/Ghent for mid Nov which appeared cheap following Cargill's fixture of Konavle earlier this week for 60,000 hss U.S. Gulf/continent for Nov 15/22 at $13.50.
A little activity was seen from the Plate with a Panamax said to have been taken for U.S. Gulf/China and Romac timechartering a 40,000 dwt vessel to the Continent at an economical rate.
Dreyfus quoted 50,000/10 meals up river completing Rio Grande/China for early Nov and Iranian interests 55,000 corn up river/Iran for Nov/Dec.

A fair number of handy fixtures were reported in the North Atlantic and in addition to these Toepfer booked about 30,000 hss Mississippi/Portugal at close to $15.50 and Continental 25,000 wheat Southampton/Tunisia, possibly at about $16.50.

MINERALS ETC--Significantly higher Caper rates were reported and rumoured today. Electicite de France paid $6.75 for about 130,000 coal Richards Bay/Sines for Dec 1/15, up from Portline's fixture at $5.65 a week ago.
A Marshal-class Caper of about 110,000 dwt was rumoured fixed Richards Bay/contine at close to $8.00.
Cobelfret was said to be trading a small Caper for ore business delivery Narvik trip via Misurata redelivery Gibraltar at between $11,500 and $12,000 daily.

Although Georgios M 148,000 dwt was believed to have fixed and failed on subjects with Pan Ocean delivery Shanghai early Dec for a trip via NSW to South Korea at $12,500 daily, it was later reported that these charterers fixed instead Stellar Cape 146,859 dwt delivery Japan for a Roberts Bank coal round at $13,000 daily.
The recent high volume of Panamax business was maintained, especially in the Pacific. It was said that short period business had been done at $11,000 daily but full details were lacking.
Meantime Kleimar fixed Alessandra d'Amato 69,171 dwt delivery Taiwan mid Feb for 2 laden legs at $10,500 daily but failed on subjects and is now said to have booked another Panamax for 3-5 months.
Navix was thought to have taken a Panamax for Goa iron ore to Japan and K Line was linked with Bunga Srigading 5,921 dwt delivery Taiwan for a coal trip via Indonesia to Japan at $10,500 daily.
Belships may have fixed Anangel Venture 69,406 dwt delivery Bin Qasim early Nov for 5-7 or 6-8 months at the same rate.
In the Atlantic Halla was said to have fixed Oriental Nova 70,000 dwt delivery Liverpool early Nov for 3-5 months redelivery Atlantic at $10,250 daily.
Continental was understood to have relet Konkar Star 69,500 dwt delivery spot Passero for a trip via U.S. Gulf with fertilizers to China to unnamed charterers.
There were reports from New York of 50,000 ferts fixed Kotka/China at $23.50 and 30,000 phosphate Tampa/Karachi by Norsk Hydro at $33.00, up a dollar from Cargill's fixture earlier this week.

A 27,000 scrap cargo Stowing 51 was reported booked USNH/South Korea at a lumpsum of $890,000. Van Ommeren fixed a 27,000 dwt U.S. Gulf/Continent and EACC a 40,000 dwt for short period in the Far East, both on private terms.
